components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one amber action in an area.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn ds-btn-primary"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linecap="round"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>Add item</button>
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 6px; font-family: 'Figtree Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; white-space: nowrap; border: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms, color 150ms, border-color 150ms, transform 150ms; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent-fill, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); color: var(--on-accent, oklch(0.22 0.03 55)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.84 0.14 74); } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outlined action beside or instead of the primary.
components.css: .ds-btn2 { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, oklch(0.56 0.03 65)); background: transparent; color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms; } .ds-btn2:hover { background: var(--raised, oklch(0.28 0.026 55)); } .ds-btn2:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn2:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chip Group
components.description: Radio or checkbox chips over hidden inputs; selected chip gets the amber border.
components.css: .ds-chips { display: flex; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Figtree Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-chips input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 1px; height: 1px; } .ds-chips span { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--line, oklch(0.36 0.026 60)); color: var(--muted, oklch(0.75 0.025 75)); font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-chips span:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong, oklch(0.56 0.03 65)); color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); } .ds-chips input:checked + span { border-color: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); background: var(--raised, oklch(0.28 0.026 55)); color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); } .ds-chips input:focus-visible + span { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: 40px field on the surface fill; 1rem text.
components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Figtree Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field span { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); } .ds-field input { height: 40px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, oklch(0.56 0.03 65)); background: var(--surface, oklch(0.235 0.022 55)); color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); font: inherit; font-size: 1rem; transition: border-color 150ms; } .ds-field input::placeholder { color: var(--muted, oklch(0.75 0.025 75)); } .ds-field input:hover { border-color: var(--muted, oklch(0.75 0.025 75)); } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Library, Pick, Log with an amber underline on the selected tab.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, oklch(0.36 0.026 60)); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-tabs button { position: relative; height: 48px; padding: 0 16px; background: none; border: 0; color: var(--muted, oklch(0.75 0.025 75)); font: inherit; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms; } .ds-tabs button:hover, .ds-tabs button[aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); } .ds-tabs button[aria-selected="true"]::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 8px; right: 8px; bottom: -1px; height: 2px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); } .ds-tabs button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Undo Toast
components.description: Bottom toast with an amber Undo action instead of a confirm dialog.
components.css: .ds-toast { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; max-width: 28rem; padding: 6px 6px 6px 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong, oklch(0.56 0.03 65)); background: var(--raised, oklch(0.28 0.026 55)); color: var(--ink, oklch(0.93 0.02 80)); font-family: 'Figtree Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; box-shadow: 0 8px 24px -8px oklch(0.1 0.02 55 / 0.5); } .ds-toast p { flex: 1; margin: 0; } .ds-toast-undo { height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: none; color: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); font: inherit; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; } .ds-toast-undo:hover { background: var(--surface, oklch(0.235 0.022 55)); text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 4px; } .ds-toast-undo:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Shelf Board with Spines
components.description: Signature: spines standing on a three-stop wooden board; hover or focus lifts a spine 6px on the overshooting pull curve with the pulled shadow.
components.css: .ds-board { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 2px; margin: 0; padding: 12px 12px 0; list-style: none; border-bottom: 14px solid var(--wood-face, oklch(0.37 0.062 52)); box-shadow: inset 0 -3px 0 var(--wood-top, oklch(0.47 0.075 60)), 0 3px 0 var(--wood-edge, oklch(0.25 0.04 48)); } .ds-spine { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 1.75rem; padding: 6px 0; border: 0; border-radius: 1.5px; background: linear-gradient(var(--b), var(--b)); color: var(--i); font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 720; font-variation-settings: 'wdth' 75, 'opsz' 14; font-size: 0.8125rem; cursor: pointer; filter: drop-shadow(0 1px 0 oklch(0.1 0.02 55 / 0.5)) drop-shadow(0 5px 5px oklch(0.1 0.02 55 / 0.4)); transition: translate 280ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.4, 0.55, 1), scale 280ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.4, 0.55, 1), filter 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-spine span { writing-mode: vertical-rl; transform: rotate(180deg); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-spine:hover, .ds-spine:focus-visible { translate: 0 -6px; filter: drop-shadow(0 1px 0 oklch(0.1 0.02 55 / 0.4)) drop-shadow(0 16px 14px oklch(0.08 0.02 55 / 0.55)); } .ds-spine:active { translate: 0 -10px; scale: 1.03; transition-duration: 120ms; } .ds-spine:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.145 72)); outline-offset: 4px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-spine, .ds-spine:hover, .ds-spine:focus-visible, .ds-spine:active { translate: none; scale: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The library looks like a wall of real shelves in the owner's home: walnut boards, things standing on them as the objects they are, a warm light falling from above onto faintly grained paper. Books show bookcloth spines with head and tail bands, board games stand as lidded boxes, video games and films sit in keep-cases behind a clear sleeve, records lean in their sleeves with the disc peeking out. You recognise the kind of thing before you read its title.

It is still a working tool. Navigation, tabs, chips, inputs, menus and dialogs are plain, flat web controls on a neutral walnut (or linen) ramp. The world lends four things: lettering, palette, density and one signature move, the spine pull-out: hovering or focusing a spine tips it forward off the board, pressing pulls it further, and it travels into the detail sheet as the full cover.

Two themes, never mixed: Stacks (dark, the default; the couch at night) and Reading Room (light; daytime at the laptop). The theme is set on <html data-theme> before first paint.
keyCharacteristics: Chrome stays flat (surface panels, hairlines, 6px corners); only objects and things that float carry shadows.
Colour lives in the objects: twelve bookcloth, jacket and sleeve hues across the whole spectrum.
Bricolage Grotesque sets names and numbers (heavy in headings, condensed on spines); Figtree sets everything you operate and read.
One accent, amber, for the primary action, the selected state and the focus ring.
Motion is physical on objects (springs, a lift that overshoots a hair) and brief everywhere else; reduced motion keeps the fades and drops the travel.
Undo toasts instead of confirm dialogs.

rules.name: The Objects Carry Color Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour belongs to covers, spines, wheel slices and confetti. Chrome stays on the neutral ramp plus amber, oxblood and moss. No new UI hues, no Tailwind palette utilities.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Within one area amber marks one thing: the primary action, the selected option, or the focused control. One amber-filled button per area.

rules.name: The Wood Is Material Rule
rules.body: Wood appears only on shelf boards and the wheel rim. It is never a panel, button or background colour.

rules.name: The Lettered Names Rule
rules.body: Bricolage sets names and numbers worth reading: the wordmark, a place, an item, a month, a date, a stat figure. It never sets a button, a field label or a paragraph; Figtree never sets a heading.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Dates, times, counts, durations, page counts and stats use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small label stacked above a heading. Counts and context sit on the heading's baseline or below it.

rules.name: The Physical-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only real objects and things that float have shadows. No glass, no backdrop blur, no glow halos on chrome. Light on objects (a sleeve's glare, a lid's sheen) is part of drawing the object, not a UI effect.

dos: Do put every chrome colour on the semantic tokens so both themes follow.
Do show an item as its object (cover or spine) wherever it appears, sized from its real aspect ratio.
Do keep Edit and Remove always visible, and undo instead of confirm.
Do give every moving thing a reduced-motion form: keep the opacity fade (about 150ms), drop the travel, the stagger and the confetti.
Do write object lift with `translate` and `scale` so it never fights the transform the shared-layout move writes.
Do make arrivals confident (ease-out-expo, 200–320ms) and exits faster than arrivals; dialogs close instantly.
Do give every spine an accessible name with the full title, kind and place.
donts: Don't make a poster-thumbnail grid the default view; the shelf is home.
Don't put shadows on chrome, or glass, backdrop blur or glow anywhere in the interface.
Don't use Tailwind palette utilities (indigo, gray, slate) or hues outside the token ramp and the object palette.
Don't set buttons, labels or paragraphs in Bricolage, or headings in Figtree.
Don't stack a small label above a heading.
Don't use tavern, pub or fantasy vocabulary in copy.
Don't use `window.confirm`, hover-only actions, or emoji as icons.
